core: Both communities embed a secondary check inside the evaluation run itself, separate from the main content being scored, whose expected outcome is already known beforehand — purely to catch problems in the evaluation apparatus (scorer or judge) rather than to measure the target agent's actual task performance. In one case this means rerunning the same test items with irrelevant metadata scrambled and confirming scores don't move; in the other it means seeding verified, previously-answered cases into batches and confirming judges score them correctly. When the check fails, the affected results are treated as unreliable and excluded or halted rather than counted toward final metrics.
quote_1: Ran a ⟦T1⟧ right after to sanity-check the scorer while we were at it. Randomized every timestamp, run id, and output filename we could find and reran the same 80 tasks.
quote_2: Each batch included a ⟦T2⟧ containing eight previously verified cases distributed without positional regularity. The ⟦T2⟧ was evaluated before aggregate metrics were retained, and three batches were halted after two known cases received unsupported negative judgments.
